_about: Theodore Roosevelt's tours, trips and expeditions. Each has an original short line and summary written by the Library. Start and end dates are anchored to day entries in the TRA Chronological Record (cited in 'anchor'): the day he set out and the day he reached home or the record's last travel day. 'verified': false means an editor has not yet confirmed the boundary against a second source.

tours.title: The Family Grand Tour of Europe
tours.short: Ten-year-old Teedie's first trip abroad, kept in his own travel diary.
tours.summary: The whole family sails on the Scotia for a year in Europe. Teedie fights asthma in London and at the seaside, walks the Black Forest, writes to Edith Carow, gets homesick, and in Rome finds himself kissing the hand of Pope Pius IX after boasting that no true American would.
tours.anchor: 1869-05-12 sails on the Scotia; 1870-05-25 home to New York

tours.title: Egypt, the Holy Land and Dresden
tours.short: A year on the Nile, in the Holy Land and in Dresden that turned a sickly boy into a collector.
tours.summary: The Roosevelts sail again, this time for Egypt. Theodore gets his first shotgun on Christmas Day aboard a Nile houseboat, shoots and skins birds all the way upriver, and helps row Ralph Waldo Emerson to lunch. The trip runs on through the Holy Land and ends with a summer living with a family in Dresden before the family comes home to a new house on 57th Street.
tours.anchor: 1872-10-16 sails on the Russia; 1873-11-05 home to 57th Street

tours.title: Prairie Hunt with Elliott
tours.short: Six weeks of bird shooting across Illinois, Iowa and Minnesota with his brother.
tours.summary: Newly engaged to Alice Lee and missing her every day, Roosevelt heads west with Elliott. The brothers shoot prairie chickens on an Illinois farm, ride the Iowa prairie by wagon, and camp on the Buffalo River near Moorhead. Elliott is the better shot, and Roosevelt says so. He tallies 404 head of game, then races home to Alice.
tours.anchor: 1880-08-16 leaves for Chicago with Elliott; 1880-09-29 back in New York

tours.title: Honeymoon in Europe with Alice
tours.short: A summer honeymoon that took him to the top of the Matterhorn.
tours.summary: Married the October before, Roosevelt and Alice sail on the Celtic for five months abroad. They tour Ireland, England and the Continent, and in the Alps he climbs the Jungfrau and the Matterhorn. News that President Garfield has been shot reaches him in the mountains; word that Garfield has died finds him in Liverpool.
tours.anchor: 1881-05-12 sails on the Celtic; 1881-10-03 met at the pier

tours.title: First Buffalo Hunt in Dakota
tours.short: The month that brought him to the Badlands and made him a rancher.
tours.summary: Roosevelt steps off the train at Little Missouri at two in the morning, hires Joe Ferris as his guide, and spends weeks soaked, thrown and lost in pursuit of a buffalo. Before he gets one, he writes a $14,000 check to go into cattle with Sylvane Ferris and Bill Merrifield at the Maltese Cross. The Badlands chapter of his life begins here.
tours.anchor: 1883-09-03 leaves New York; 1883-10-02 last leg home

tours.title: A London Wedding and a Winter in Europe
tours.short: Across the Atlantic to marry Edith Carow, and a winter abroad as newlyweds.
tours.summary: Roosevelt sails on the Etruria with his sister Bamie, makes a lifelong friend of Cecil Spring Rice on board, and marries Edith at St. George's Church in London on a day so foggy the mist fills the church. The newlyweds spend the winter on the Continent and come home in March to three-year-old Alice, waiting in her best sash.
tours.anchor: 1886-11-06 sails for England; 1887-03-28 home in New York

tours.title: Hunting the Kootenai Country
tours.short: A hard hunt in the mountains of Idaho and British Columbia.
tours.summary: From the Badlands Roosevelt goes north and west to the Kootenai country with guide John Willis. Most of his companions give up after a week. He stays on, and comes out with a bear and a caribou.
tours.anchor: 1888-08-26 bound for Idaho; 1888-10-04 eastbound for home

tours.title: The Roosevelt Special
tours.short: The whistle-stop train that carried the Rough Rider to the governor's office.
tours.summary: Weeks out of uniform, Roosevelt crosses New York State on a campaign train with Rough Riders and reporters aboard. He takes on Richard Croker and the Tammany machine in town after town, turns 40 giving 14 speeches in a day, and is elected governor the day after his last swing through the Southern Tier.
tours.anchor: 1898-10-17 whistle-stopping up the Hudson; 1898-11-07 last Southern Tier swing

tours.title: West to the First Rough Rider Reunion
tours.short: Governor Roosevelt goes to Las Vegas, New Mexico, for the regiment's first reunion.
tours.summary: A week on the rails to rejoin his Rough Riders for their first reunion, with a parade and a memorial service for the men they lost. On the way home he speaks in Illinois and Milwaukee, then tells reporters he is not a candidate for President in 1900.
tours.anchor: 1899-06-21 leaves Ithaca for the West; 1899-06-29 back in Albany

tours.title: The 1900 Campaign Train
tours.short: Two months on the stump as McKinley's running mate, from Michigan to Montana and back.
tours.summary: As the Republican candidate for Vice President, Roosevelt carries the campaign west on a long rail tour: Labor Day in Chicago, eleven speeches in a day in Michigan, an afternoon back in Medora, and a rough reception in Colorado's Cripple Creek mining district. He ends with a rain-soaked rally at Madison Square Garden three days before the election.
tours.anchor: 1900-09-02 bound for Chicago; 1900-11-03 final rally at Madison Square Garden

tours.title: Cougar Hunt in Colorado
tours.short: The Vice President-elect's winter hunt for mountain lions in the Colorado snow.
tours.summary: Before taking office, Roosevelt rides out of Meeker with hunter John Goff and his hounds for five weeks of cougar and lynx hunting in deep snow. Several of the big cats he finishes with a knife while the dogs hold them. The biggest weighs 227 pounds.
tours.anchor: 1901-01-07 leaves to hunt cougar; 1901-02-23 home to Sagamore Hill

tours.title: New England Tour
tours.short: A swing through six New England states that ended in a trolley crash.
tours.summary: President Roosevelt takes his case against the trusts to New England, speaking from Connecticut to Maine and on through New Hampshire and Vermont. In Pittsfield, Massachusetts, a streetcar slams into his carriage. Secret Service agent William Craig is killed, and Roosevelt's leg is badly hurt.
tours.anchor: 1902-08-22 Hartford; 1902-09-03 trolley crash at Pittsfield

tours.title: Wheeling, Chattanooga and North Carolina
tours.short: A short trip south only days after the Pittsfield crash.
tours.summary: Still bruised, Roosevelt speaks on the trusts at Wheeling, reviews cavalry and walks the battlefield at Chattanooga, addresses the locomotive firemen's convention, and speaks in Asheville and Greensboro on the way home.
tours.anchor: 1902-09-05 leaves for Chattanooga; 1902-09-10 back to Oyster Bay

tours.title: Midwestern Tour, Cut Short
tours.short: A western tour that lasted five days.
tours.summary: Roosevelt heads west with the coal strike unresolved, speaking in Cincinnati and Detroit. In Indianapolis doctors find that the leg hurt at Pittsfield needs surgery. The tour is called off, and he is carried into the temporary White House on Jackson Place to rest.
tours.anchor: 1902-09-19 starts west; 1902-09-23 surgery in Indianapolis; 1902-09-24 resting in Washington

tours.title: The Mississippi Bear Hunt
tours.short: The hunt that gave the teddy bear its name.
tours.summary: Roosevelt goes after bear in the canebrakes near Smedes, Mississippi. The newspapers carry the story that he would not shoot a bear that had been run down and tied for him, and a cartoon called Drawing the Line in Mississippi spreads it everywhere.
tours.anchor: 1902-11-12 southbound; 1902-11-20 whistle stops home

tours.title: The Great Western Tour
tours.short: Nine weeks across the West: the longest trip of his presidency.
tours.summary: Roosevelt leaves Washington for the longest trip of his presidency. He stops in the Badlands to see old friends, camps two weeks in Yellowstone with John Burroughs, dedicates the St. Louis World's Fair grounds, stands at the edge of the Grand Canyon, and sleeps under the sequoias and in the snow of Yosemite with John Muir. He rides 65 miles on horseback from Laramie to Cheyenne before heading home.
tours.anchor: 1903-04-01 tour begins; 1903-06-05 home

tours.title: Texas, Oklahoma and Colorado Hunt
tours.short: A Rough Rider reunion in Texas, a coyote hunt in Oklahoma and a bear hunt in Colorado.
tours.summary: Early in his second term, Roosevelt speaks to the Texas Legislature and his Rough Riders in San Antonio, then gallops after coyotes with greyhounds in Oklahoma alongside Jack Abernathy. He finishes with weeks of bear hunting in the Colorado mountains, cutting it short as Japan and Russia move toward peace talks.
tours.anchor: 1905-04-03 leaves Washington; 1905-05-11 home by midnight

tours.title: The Southern Tour
tours.short: Through the South to his mother's girlhood home, and back by sea.
tours.summary: With Edith along, Roosevelt speaks his way through Virginia, the Carolinas, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Arkansas and Louisiana. He visits Bulloch Hall in Roswell, where his mother grew up, speaks at Tuskegee, and denounces lynching in Little Rock before sailing home from New Orleans on the West Virginia.
tours.anchor: 1905-10-18 leaves Washington; 1905-10-31 back at the White House

tours.title: Panama and Puerto Rico
tours.short: The first trip abroad by a sitting President: to see the canal being dug.
tours.summary: Roosevelt and Edith sail south on the battleship Louisiana to see the Panama Canal works for themselves. In a steady rain he rides across the isthmus, spends eighteen hours on his feet among the workers, and climbs into the cab of a steam shovel at Culebra. They stop in Puerto Rico on the way home.
tours.anchor: 1906-11-08 sails on the Louisiana; 1906-11-25 last day at sea

tours.title: Down the Mississippi
tours.short: Down the great river by steamboat, into the Louisiana canebrakes, and home to a panic.
tours.summary: Roosevelt dedicates the McKinley Memorial in Canton, then boards a stern-wheeler at Keokuk for his first trip down the Mississippi, leading a fleet of steamers and speaking for a deeper waterway. He spends two weeks after bear on the Tensas in Louisiana and gets one on the twelfth day. He reaches Washington as the Panic of 1907 breaks.
tours.anchor: 1907-09-29 leaves for a three-week tour; 1907-10-23 home to the Panic

tours.title: Smithsonian-Roosevelt African Expedition
tours.short: A year collecting for the Smithsonian across East Africa and down the Nile.
tours.summary: Days out of office, Roosevelt sails with Kermit for British East Africa. From Mombasa they ride the railroad into the game country and spend the year hunting and collecting specimens for the Smithsonian across what are now Kenya and Uganda, then travel down the Nile to Khartoum, where Edith and Ethel are waiting.
tours.anchor: 1909-03-23 sails on the Hamburg; 1910-03-14 meets Edith at Khartoum

tours.title: From Khartoum to London
tours.short: From Khartoum to London, with the most famous speeches of his life.
tours.summary: Reunited with Edith, Roosevelt travels from Egypt through Italy, Austria-Hungary, France, the Low Countries, Scandinavia, Germany and Britain. He gives Citizenship in a Republic at the Sorbonne, delivers his Nobel lecture in Christiania, reviews the German army beside the Kaiser, and speaks his mind on Egypt at London's Guildhall. New York gives him a hero's welcome home.
tours.anchor: 1910-03-15 speaks at Khartoum; 1910-06-18 welcomed home in New York

tours.title: Western Tour and the New Nationalism
tours.short: A sixteen-state tour and the New Nationalism.
tours.summary: Back from abroad and pulled into politics, Roosevelt heads west in a private car. In Osawatomie, Kansas, he delivers The New Nationalism, the most important speech of his life after the presidency. He also tells a crowd in Sioux Falls that his years on a Dakota ranch were the most important part of his education.
tours.anchor: 1910-08-23 tour begins; 1910-09-11 home

tours.title: The 34-Day Tour of 1911
tours.short: Thirty-four days across the South and the West, with Edith and Ethel.
tours.summary: Roosevelt speaks his way from Atlanta through Texas to Arizona, where he rides into the Grand Canyon with Archie and dedicates the dam on the Salt River that bears his name. At Berkeley he gives the Earl Lectures and the speech with his famous line about taking the Isthmus, and comes home through the Pacific Northwest and Montana.
tours.anchor: 1911-03-08 leaves on a 34-day tour; 1911-04-16 home to Oyster Bay

tours.title: Coast to Coast for the Bull Moose
tours.short: A month crossing the country as the Progressive candidate for President.
tours.summary: From Connecticut to California and back through the South, Roosevelt takes the Bull Moose campaign to the whole country. He draws some 50,000 at the Minnesota State Fair, answers Woodrow Wilson's New Freedom in San Francisco, sees crowds line the streets of Los Angeles, and visits his mother's girlhood home in Roswell after hecklers disrupt his speech in Atlanta.
tours.anchor: 1912-09-02 Connecticut kickoff; 1912-10-02 home to Sagamore Hill

tours.title: The Great Lakes Tour and Milwaukee
tours.short: The campaign tour that ended with a bullet in Milwaukee.
tours.summary: Roosevelt sets out across Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin with his voice wearing out. In Milwaukee, outside the Gilpatrick Hotel, he is shot in the chest by John Schrank. He gives his speech anyway, then spends a week in Chicago's Mercy Hospital before going home to Sagamore Hill.
tours.anchor: 1912-10-07 leaves on a Great Lakes tour; 1912-10-14 shot in Milwaukee; 1912-10-22 home

tours.title: Grand Canyon, Rainbow Bridge and the Hopi Mesas
tours.short: Seven weeks in the canyon country with his sons Archie and Quentin.
tours.summary: Roosevelt goes down the Bright Angel Trail and up to the North Rim, hunts cougars along the rim with his sons and cousin Nicholas, rides through the desert to Lees Ferry and Navajo country, camps beneath Rainbow Bridge, and watches the Hopi snake dance at Walpi.
tours.anchor: 1913-07-07 leaves with Archie and Quentin; 1913-08-26 home

tours.title: South America and the River of Doubt
tours.short: A speaking tour that became the descent of the River of Doubt.
tours.summary: Roosevelt sails for South America to lecture, then joins Brazilian explorer Cândido Rondon to trace an unmapped river through the Amazon basin. On the River of Doubt the party loses men and canoes, Roosevelt nearly dies of an infected leg and fever, and the river is renamed the Rio Roosevelt.
tours.anchor: 1913-10-04 sails on the Vandyck; 1914-05-19 homecoming

tours.title: Madrid and London for Kermit's Wedding
tours.short: Across the Atlantic for Kermit's wedding in Madrid.
tours.summary: Barely home from Brazil, Roosevelt sails with Alice for Spain. He lunches with King Alfonso XIII, sees Kermit marry Belle Willard in Madrid, and goes on to London to speak to the Royal Geographical Society about the River of Doubt.

tours.title: West to the Expositions
tours.short: West by the Canadian Rockies to the expositions, preaching preparedness.
tours.summary: With war in Europe, Roosevelt crosses Canada to the Pacific and travels down to San Francisco for a Roosevelt Day at the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, then on to San Diego's exposition. At every stop his theme is national preparedness.
tours.anchor: 1915-07-11 off to California; 1915-08-02 back in New York

tours.title: The West Indies
tours.short: Six weeks in the Caribbean, and a statement from Trinidad.
tours.summary: Roosevelt and Edith sail for a holiday in the islands. They call at Guadeloupe, Barbados and Trinidad. From Port of Spain he tells reporters he is not seeking the Republican nomination. He sails home alone on the Matura while Edith stays on.
tours.anchor: 1916-02-11 sails; 1916-03-24 home from Trinidad

tours.title: Western Swing for Hughes
tours.short: A western swing campaigning for Charles Evans Hughes.
tours.summary: With three reporters along for the ride, Roosevelt stumps for the Republican nominee through Kentucky, Indiana, Kansas, Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado and Illinois, telling stories and pointing out wildlife from the train between stops.
tours.anchor: 1916-10-17 western swing begins; 1916-10-28 Brooklyn

tours.title: Devilfishing in Florida
tours.short: Harpooning giant rays in the Gulf as the country goes to war.
tours.summary: Roosevelt goes to Punta Gorda to hunt devilfish with harpoon expert Russell Coles. On the way home he stops in Washington on the day President Wilson asks Congress to declare war.
tours.anchor: 1917-03-23 leaves for Florida; 1917-04-03 back in New York
